advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a liveness anchor to test_inbound_only_batch_makes_no_jira_write proving reroute_migrated_plans actually processed the inbound plan (e.g. assert _production_plans returned a non-empty plan carrying the inbound mutation, or spy that the reroute/batch path was invoked) before trusting the no-write absence.
evidence: Both assertions are absence-only; there is no outbound mutation in this batch and no presence assertion anywhere, so no producer liveness is established (fail-open oracle).

ticket_planner.plan_pass can legitimately exclude a target (src/rebar/reconciler/ticket_planner.py:301-312 `_classify_early` / mode-cap / disposition), in which case the inbound mutation never reaches reroute_migrated_plans and the test still passes.
advisory.finding: test_inbound_only_batch_makes_no_jira_write asserts only absences (update_issue.call_args_list == [] and add_comment.call_args_list == []) with no liveness anchor that the inbound plan actually reached reroute_migrated_plans and was rejected there. It passes identically whether the new guard correctly skips the inbound-only plan OR _production_plans/ticket_planner.plan_pass filtered the plan upstream (e.g. via _classify_early / mode-cap / non-mutate disposition) so the reroute code never ran. The inbound-only case is the simplest regression the diff introduces, yet this test cannot distinguish a working guard from a no-op setup.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert `_production_plans([inbound])` is non-empty and that the resulting plan contains the inbound mutation, or assert the batch/reroute path was entered, before the `== []` checks.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a producer-liveness anchor (e.g. assert update_issue fired for the outbound DIG-2) to test_inbound_jira_comment_is_not_posted_back_to_jira before trusting add_comment.call_args_list == [].
evidence: The only comment-bearing mutation is the inbound one (comments=({'body': 'comment that came from Jira'},)); the outbound DIG-2 update carries no comment, so add_comment==[] is the expected result of ANY path, working or dead.
advisory.finding: test_inbound_jira_comment_is_not_posted_back_to_jira asserts only add_comment.call_args_list == [] but its single outbound mutation (DIG-2 OutboundUpdatePayload) carries no comment, so add_comment would be empty even in a fully working outbound path and even if the batch never dispatched. The test has no presence anchor (it does not assert DIG-2's update_issue fired), so it cannot distinguish 'inbound comment correctly skipped' from 'machinery never ran'.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `assert [c.args[0] for c in client.update_issue.call_args_list] == ['DIG-2']` before the add_comment absence assertion, matching the anchor already used in test_inbound_update_is_not_written_back_to_jira.
